title: Once upon a time, and then
goal: Follow the tenses of a story, read long narrative sentences built with -(y)Ip and -(y)ArAk, and recognize literary forms such as gidesim geldi.

intro.text: A story picks a base tense: `-DI` if the narrator was there, `-mIş` if it was heard, the present to bring a scene close. One finite verb can end a whole chain of `-(y)Ip` and `-(y)ArAk`. Literature also keeps older forms: *gidesim geldi* is **I felt like going**.

vocab.en: and then, just then (in a story)
time went by, as time passed (in tales)
life far from home, abroad (gurbette: far from home)
longing, missing someone (hasret çekmek: to long for)
to feel like going (gidesim geldi: I felt like going; also with other verbs: ağlayası gelmek)
to death, deadly (ölesiye yorgun: dead tired)

exercises.question: A narrator writes: *Dedem gençken İstanbul'a gelmiş, bir fırında çalışmış.* Why `-mIş`?
options: The narrator wasn't there: it is family history they were told
The narrator thinks it isn't true

why.1: There is no tale formula, and the grandfather is a real person.
why.2: Here `-mIş` marks what the narrator didn't see, not doubt.
why.3: `-mIş` says nothing about how long ago it was.

exercises.explain: `-mIş` is the natural base for a past the narrator knows only from others, such as the years before they were born.

exercises.label: *gitmek* → *gidesi gelmek* in the past: **I felt like going**, you felt like going…

accept: gidesim geldi
gidesin geldi
gidesi geldi
gidesimiz geldi
gidesiniz geldi

exercises.explain: The possessive shows the person (*gidesi-m*, *gidesi-n*, *gidesi*); *gelmek* stays in the third person: never *gidesim geldim*.

accept: Suddenly she felt like crying.
Suddenly he felt like crying
[She|He] suddenly felt like crying
All of a sudden [she|he] felt like crying
Suddenly [she|he] wanted to cry
[She|He] suddenly wanted to cry
Suddenly [she|he] felt the urge to cry
[She|He] suddenly felt the urge to cry
exercises.explain: *Ağla-y-ası geldi*: the wish to cry came over her. Without a context, *o* is he or she.

exercises.gloss: my wish to go (gidesim geldi: I felt like going)
exercises.explain: *Git-* softens to *gid-* before a vowel; `-(y)AsI` takes front harmony, *-esi*; the first-person possessive after a vowel is *-m*.

exercises.prompt: Time went by, and the girl grew up.
accept: Gel zaman git zaman, kız büyüdü.
Gel zaman git zaman kız büyümüş.
[Zaman geçti|Aradan zaman geçti] (ve) kız [büyüdü|büyümüş].
exercises.explain: *Gel zaman git zaman* is the tale formula for time passing. In a folk tale, the verb would be `-mIş`: *kız büyümüş*.

exercises.question: Why does the second sentence switch to the present?

context.tr: Kapıyı açtım, bir de ne göreyim! Salonda bütün arkadaşlarım bekliyor, ellerinde bir pasta.
context.en: I opened the door, and what do I see! All my friends are waiting in the living room, a cake in their hands.

options: To make the surprise happen before the reader's eyes
Because the friends are still waiting now
Because the narrator only heard about it

why.1: The scene is in the past (*açtım*); the present only makes it vivid.
why.3: A habit would take the aorist or `-(I)rdI`.

exercises.explain: This is the historical present. *Bir de ne göreyim!* (and what do I see!) is a storyteller's formula that often comes just before it.

exercises.prompt: Bütün gece doyasıya konuştuk ve sabaha dek uyumadık.
accept: We talked to our heart's content all night and didn't sleep until morning.
We talked to our heart's content all night and did not sleep until the morning
We talked to our heart's content all night and never slept until (the) morning
We talked to our heart's content all night long and [did not sleep|never slept] until (the) morning
We talked to our hearts' content all night (long) and [did not sleep|never slept] until (the) morning
All night (long) we talked to our [heart's|hearts'] content and [did not sleep|never slept] until (the) morning
We talked all night to our [heart's|hearts'] content and [did not sleep|never slept] until (the) morning
We talked [as much as we wanted|our fill] all night (long) and [did not sleep|never slept] until (the) morning
exercises.explain: *Doyasıya* (until full) is **to your heart's content**; *dek* is the written word for *kadar*.

exercises.tr: Gel zaman git zaman, kız büyümüş.
exercises.en: Time went by, and the girl grew up.

exercises.task: Rewrite this paragraph as family history the narrator was told rather than saw: change every finite verb to `-mIş`. If you like, join two sentences with `-(y)Ip` and frame the story with *anlatılanlara göre*.
exercises.source: Dedem 1950'de Trabzon'dan İstanbul'a geldi. Önce bir fırında çalıştı, sonra kendi dükkânını açtı. Babam o dükkânın üstündeki evde doğdu.
models: Dedem 1950'de Trabzon'dan İstanbul'a gelmiş. Önce bir fırında çalışmış, sonra kendi dükkânını açmış. Babam o dükkânın üstündeki evde doğmuş.
Anlatılanlara göre dedem 1950'de Trabzon'dan İstanbul'a gelmiş; önce bir fırında çalışıp sonra kendi dükkânını açmış. Babam da o dükkânın üstündeki evde doğmuş.
checklist: A chain with `-(y)Ip`, if you made one, has no tense of its own: *çalışıp … açmış*
Optional: a frame such as *anlatılanlara göre*
